title: Degree-zero Tate powers and detection of automorphisms
statement: Fix a finite purity datum P [def-pur-conventions], a finite-type k-scheme X with its specified structure morphism aX:X->Spec(k) and r in N. Let T_X be the actual comparison-origin finite Tate power Lambda_X(r)[2r], and L_X=T_X[-2r] [def-pur-composition-model-orientation-coordinates]. Then L_X has homology concentrated in degree zero, and H^0(L_X), realized as a module over the constant finite coefficient ring sheaf, is locally free of rank one. For every index type I and family of Zariski opens U_i of X with supremum top, the map Aut(T_X) -> product_i Aut(T_X|_(U_i)) given by the exact derived open restrictions is injective. This includes the empty covering of the empty scheme.

proof.text: The degree-zero sheaf $L=\Lambda_X(d+e)$ is locally free of rank one: take a local basis of the finite Tate line and tensor it $d+e$ times, using $1\otimes\cdots\otimes1\mapsto1$ as basis, and the coefficient unit if $d+e=0$. On these trivializations tensor is the identity functor on module sheaves, so the ordinary tensor powers represent the derived powers. Thus $T_X=L[2d+2e]$. Shift removal sends an endomorphism of $T_X$ to an endomorphism of $L[0]$, and shifting back is its inverse; these operations commute with exact open restriction. Apply degree-zero derived-map gluing with $M=N=L[0]$ and the open covering of Step 6. Its concentration hypothesis holds since $L$ is a sheaf in degree zero. The injectivity part says two endomorphisms of $L[0]$ with equal restrictions coincide. Shifting back proves injectivity of the restriction on endomorphisms of $T_X$, hence on its automorphisms. This uses no gluing assertion for arbitrary derived complexes.
